desc.C: A halal certificate is recorded for this place.
desc.O: Reported to serve only halal food.
desc.Y: Reported to serve halal food. Non-halal food may also be served.
desc.F: Listed as Muslim-friendly by an official tourism organisation. Usually offers halal or pork-free dishes; alcohol may be served.
desc.L: Reported to have a few halal options.
desc.Uname: Its name or category suggests halal options. Ask the staff before you order.
desc.Ucuisine: It is listed because this cuisine is usually halal in Korea (for example Turkish, Uzbek or Pakistani). Ask the staff before you order.
desc.V: Everything on the menu is vegetarian: no meat or fish, though dairy and eggs may be used. Not halal-certified: ask about alcohol in sauces, such as cooking wine.
desc.VV: Everything on the menu is vegan: no meat, fish, dairy or eggs. Not halal-certified: ask about alcohol in sauces, such as cooking wine.
desc.M: Serves some vegetarian dishes, but meat is cooked here too, so pans and oil may be shared. Not halal-certified.
desc.MV: Serves some vegan dishes, but meat is cooked here too, so pans and oil may be shared. Not halal-certified.

brandNote.lotteria: The patty is 100% plant-based. The listed allergens are wheat, soy and tomato, with no egg or milk.
brandNote.papajohns: The Green Eat pizzas use vegan cheese (large size, original crust). The Margherita and the Garden Special are not on the official list of dishes that contain meat.
brandNote.subway: The Veggie is bread with seven vegetables; the Egg Mayo has egg and mayonnaise. Neither has meat. Skip cheese and creamy sauces if you avoid dairy.
brandNote.dominos: The official allergen table lists tomato, soy and milk, and no meat.
brandNote.salady: Marked vegan on the official menu.
brandNote.bonjuk: The official allergen list (October 2026) shows no meat, milk or egg in these porridges, not even as cross-contact. Other porridges such as the vegetable porridge contain beef.
brandNote.pizzaschool: The allergen lists on the official menu pages show milk, soy, wheat, tomato and egg, and no meat. Other pizzas, such as the truffle potato, contain ham.
brandNote.pizzamaru: The official allergen list (January 2026) shows milk, soy, wheat and tomato and no meat for these pizzas with the regular crust. Special crusts can add egg or shrimp.
brandNote.starbucks: The allergen information on the official product pages lists soy, milk and wheat (and tomato), and no meat. Other sandwiches, even ones with vegetable names, contain ham.

guide.title: Eating halal in Korea
guide.levelsIntro: Each place on the map shows how sure we are that its food is halal. Always check with the restaurant: menus and owners change.
guide.ktoBody: Korean tourism organisations sort Muslim-friendly restaurants into four levels: Halal certified (certificate from the Korea Muslim Federation, KMF), Self-certified (Muslim owner, no pork or alcohol), Muslim-friendly (halal dishes, alcohol may be served) and Pork-free (no pork, but meat is not halal). Look for these signs at the entrance.
guide.ktoLink: Korea Tourism Organization's list of Muslim-friendly restaurants (PDF)
guide.vegIntro: Square markers show vegetarian and vegan places, useful when there is no halal restaurant nearby. Meat-free food avoids the main halal concern, but it is not certified: sauces can contain alcohol.
guide.foodIntro: Many Korean dishes contain pork or alcohol even when you cannot see it. Recipes vary between restaurants, so always ask.
guide.meatNote: Beef, chicken and lamb are only halal at halal-certified or Muslim-owned restaurants. Korean fried chicken, bulgogi and galbi are usually not halal.
guide.chainsIntro: Every branch of these chains in Korea is on the map with a vegetarian marker. The dishes have no meat but are not halal-certified: grills and frying oil may be shared.
guide.phrasesIntro: Tap a phrase to show it in large letters.
guide.cardIntro: Show this card to the staff when you order.

about.title: About Muslimfood
about.body: Muslimfood helps you find halal and Muslim-friendly food quickly, wherever you are. It works on any phone, needs no account and keeps working with a weak connection.
about.disclaimer: Halal status comes from community contributors and public data. It can change at any time, so please confirm with the restaurant.
about.osm: Restaurants, mosques and prayer rooms worldwide from OpenStreetMap, © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
about.map: Map tiles: OpenFreeMap, OpenMapTiles, © OpenStreetMap contributors.
about.privacy: Your location is used only on your device to sort places by distance. This site sets no cookies and shows no ads.
about.addBody: The map is built on OpenStreetMap, which anyone can edit. Add the restaurant and tag it diet:halal=yes (some halal dishes) or diet:halal=only (everything halal). Your change appears here within a day.
about.privacyCounts: To learn what helps, we count visits and button taps anonymously with GoatCounter: no cookies and nothing that identifies you. “Do Not Track” is respected. Votes and forms you send are read by the maintainers; contact details are never published.
about.privacyNoCounts: No usage statistics are collected. Votes and forms you send are read by the maintainers; contact details are never published.

legend.title: How to read the map
legend.cert: Circle with a gold dot: halal certificate
legend.halal: Green circle: halal food (owner or tourism office)
legend.unconfirmed: Dashed circle: not confirmed, ask the staff
legend.veg: Square with a leaf: vegetarian or vegan option, not halal

owner.title: Add a restaurant
owner.intro: Run a halal restaurant, or know one that is missing? Send it here. We check every entry before it appears on the map, usually within a few days.
owner.name: Restaurant name
owner.addressHint: Naver, Kakao or Google Maps link
owner.contactHint: Only to ask you a question. Never shown on the site.
owner.notesHint: Prayer space, halal menu items, opening hours…
owner.consent: I agree that the restaurant details (not my contact) are published on Muslimfood and OpenStreetMap.
owner.missing: Please fill in the name, address and halal level, and tick the box.
owner.error: Sending failed. Check your connection and try again, or:
owner.thanksBody: We will check the details and add the restaurant, usually within a few days.
owner.thanksGithub: A GitHub page opened with your details filled in. Press “Create” there to send them.
